CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Bengkayang Regency. 2. Regional Government is Bengkayang Regency as an element of regional government administration that leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Bengkayang Regency. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the people's representative institution of Bengkayang Regency Region as an element of Regional Government administration. 5. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person recognized by law as a woman. 6. Child's Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government and regional government. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb. 8. Child with Special Needs is a child with special characteristics different from children in general without always indicating mental, emotional or physical disability, which includes among others: visually impaired, hearing impaired, mentally disabled, physically disabled, socially maladjusted, learning difficulties, behavioral disorders, gifted children, children with health disorders and disabled children. 9. Child Protection is all forms of activities to guarantee and protect children so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, as well as receive protection from violence and discrimination. 10. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substances (drugs) abuse, children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and children victims of maltreatment and neglect. 11. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community. 12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 13. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions. 14. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 15. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, as well as receive protection from violence and discrimination. 16. Implementation of protection is a series of activities aimed at: preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center. 17. Violence is any act that results or will result in misery and suffering both physical, sexual, psychological including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life. 18. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 19. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic exploitation, socially including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 20. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 21. Prevention is direct efforts made by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children. 22. Complaint is notification either in writing or orally by interested parties to authorized institutions, in which the person concerned suffers losses due to the actions of others. 23. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence. 24. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for women and children victims of violence carried out jointly by related agencies or institutions as one unified implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children. 25.

I. GENERAL
As we have known together that the protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays needs to receive serious attention, specifically Bengkayang Regency in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, this matter is as contained in the Medium-Term Development Plan of Bengkayang Regency.
This matter is to provide understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially in the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, likewise acts of violence and exploitation against children. Therefore it is expected specifically that women can know and understand various aspects regarding domestic violence.
As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as forms of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so that they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity.
Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Bengkayang Regency are very high on average per semester reaching 17 (seventeen) cases, this shows that Women's Empowerment in Bengkayang Regency in handling cases of acts of violence against women and children must receive very serious handling and attention.
Related to this matter the Bengkayang Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection of Women And Children Victims of Violence that regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children as well as where to request protection.

Article 22
(1) The Regent implements control, guidance, and supervision of the implementation of protection for victims of violence against women and children.
(2) Control, guidance, and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by the SKPD responsible for women's empowerment and child protection.

Article 12
(1) Prevention efforts as referred to in Article 11 letter a include:
a. establishing a network for prevention and handling of violence through coordination, integration, synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns;
b. establishing a violence prevention system, mapping of locations or areas prone to violence;
c. organizing communication, information, and education about violence against women and children; and
d. socialization of laws and regulations related to violence against women and children.
(2) Prevention efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out in an integrated manner coordinated by the SKPD that has duties and functions in the field of women's empowerment.

Article 18
Monitoring and reporting as referred to in Article 11 letter f, includes monitoring, documentation, and reporting of cases of violence against women and children.

Article 12
(1) Prevention efforts as referred to in Article 11 letter a include:
a. establishing a network for prevention and handling of violence through coordination, integration, synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns;
b. establishing a violence prevention system, mapping of locations or areas prone to violence;
c. organizing communication, information, and education about violence against women and children; and

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Bengkayang Regency. 2. Regional Government is Bengkayang Regency as an element of regional government administration that leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Bengkayang Regency. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the people's representative institution of Bengkayang Regency Region as an element of Regional Government administration. 5. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person recognized by law as a woman. 6. Child's Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government and regional government. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb. 8. Child with Special Needs is a child with special characteristics different from children in general without always indicating mental, emotional or physical disability, which includes among others: visually impaired, hearing impaired, mentally disabled, physically disabled, socially maladjusted, learning difficulties, behavioral disorders, gifted children, children with health disorders and disabled children. 9. Child Protection is all forms of activities to guarantee and protect children so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, as well as receive protection from violence and discrimination. 10. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substances (drugs) abuse, children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and children victims of maltreatment and neglect. 11. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community. 12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 13. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions. 14. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 15. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, as well as receive protection from violence and discrimination. 16. Implementation of protection is a series of activities aimed at: preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center. 17. Violence is any act that results or will result in misery and suffering both physical, sexual, psychological including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life. 18. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 19. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic exploitation, socially including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 20. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 21. Prevention is direct efforts made by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children. 22. Complaint is notification either in writing or orally by interested parties to authorized institutions, in which the person concerned suffers losses due to the actions of others. 23. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence. 24. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for women and children victims of violence carried out jointly by related agencies or institutions as one unified implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children. 25.

Article 22
(1) The Regent implements control, guidance, and supervision of the implementation of protection for victims of violence against women and children.
(2) Control, guidance, and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by the SKPD responsible for women's empowerment and child protection.

Article 19
(1) In providing protection for victims of violence against women and children, the Regional Government may cooperate with the Government, Provincial Government, other regional governments and other institutions.
(2) Cooperation between the Regional Government and the Government includes consultation, coordination, and reporting.
(3) Cooperation with other regional governments and other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) includes coordination, advocacy, referral, repatriation, social reintegration, and development of integrated service systems.

CHAPTER III
SCOPE
Article 4
The scope of protection for women and children victims of violence includes the rights of victims, the obligations and authority of the Regional Government, the implementation of protection, reporting, control, guidance, and supervision, community participation, and financing.

I. GENERAL
As we have known together that the protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays needs to receive serious attention, specifically Bengkayang Regency in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, this matter is as contained in the Medium-Term Development Plan of Bengkayang Regency.
This matter is to provide understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially in the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, likewise acts of violence and exploitation against children. Therefore it is expected specifically that women can know and understand various aspects regarding domestic violence.
As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as forms of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so that they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity.
Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Bengkayang Regency are very high on average per semester reaching 17 (seventeen) cases, this shows that Women's Empowerment in Bengkayang Regency in handling cases of acts of violence against women and children must receive very serious handling and attention.
Related to this matter the Bengkayang Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection of Women And Children Victims of Violence that regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children as well as where to request protection.

Article 18
Monitoring and reporting as referred to in Article 11 letter f, includes monitoring, documentation, and reporting of cases of violence against women and children.

Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs. 33. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.

5.3.rationale: The original Indonesian text Pasal 17 huruf c says “menumbuhkan kearifan lokal dalam penanganan terhadap perempuan dan anak korban kekerasan” (fostering local wisdom in handling cases). This is a general statement about using local wisdom, but it does not clearly specify engagement with traditional/cultural leaders, customary institutions, or concrete cultural/traditional mechanisms (e.g., adat councils, tokoh adat, religious/traditional authorities) as stakeholders. The judge inferred ‘traditional/cultural engagement’ from the phrase alone, which may be too expansive for this indicator if it requires explicit stakeholder engagement structures. The information was available, but the judge’s interpretation likely overreached.
